title: Künneth–Verdier isomorphism
statement:
The three maps of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps] are isomorphisms, natural in their
variables, under the hypotheses of that definition (the $Rf_i^!$ are the
constructible exceptional adjoints of [sk-def-sf-operations] (vi); no
admissibility datum of [sk-def-sf-admissible] is assumed): the
exceptional Künneth map $\alpha$, the external Hom map $\beta$, and the
Künneth–Verdier map $\kappa$. In particular, for $X,Y$ separated of finite
type over $k$, with the structure
morphism $a_Y$ and the product projection $p_X=\operatorname{id}_X\times a_Y$
as in [sk-def-sf-kv-maps] (iv), and
$M\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, $N\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$,

$$
\kappa_{M,N}:M\boxtimes\mathbb D_YN\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\
\RHom\bigl(p_Y^*N,Rp_X^!M\bigr).
$$

source.place: node sk-thm-sf-kunneth-verdier, order 2512

proof.text: Work first with A=A_{E,n} and separated finite-type k-schemes. All inputs and intermediate values lie in D^b_ctf by [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i)-(v). Write P_f=Rf_! and G_f=Rf^! for the actual constructible adjoints of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi). Compact-support composition [thm-sf-comp-composition] and conjugacy [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] identify G_{gf}=G_f G_g. The composite counit is epsilon_g composed with P_g(epsilon_f), by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2); the same statement supplies identity normalization. These are actual exceptional adjoints, with no ambient admissibility assumption. Open restriction below extends the argument to nonseparated finite-type corners.

source.place: alpha: actual adjunctions and composition

proof.text: Verify the finite datum [def-sf-datum] needed for site-perfect evaluation. A1: ordinary adjunction is [fix-prop-adjunctions](1), exceptional adjunction is [sk-def-sf-operations](vi), and the composite counits are those of Step 1. A2: [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives an etale-origin witness for every input, so [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] supplies compact-support base change. For proper f the identity-open compactification identifies Rf_! with Rf_*, giving proper ordinary base change as well; smooth ordinary base change is [fix-lem-exchanges](3). A3 is precisely [fix-prop-projection-formula].

source.place: finite concrete datum: axioms A1-A3

proof.text: A4 of [def-sf-datum] is [thm-sf-comp-composition] with its pentagon and the identity-open compactification for proper maps. A5 follows on the stated finite-Tor domains from [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii), [lem-fix-operation-reduction] and [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(2),(4): these state compatibility of the operations, evaluations and adjunction maps with the coefficient constructions. A6 is the geometric exact biduality of [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vi). Thus all six required clauses of the finite datum have been checked, rather than treating its defining axioms as theorems.

source.place: finite concrete datum: axioms A4-A6

proof.text: Use [lem-sf-kv-alpha-transpose-coherence] to compose the specified alpha maps under G_{gf}=G_f G_g, and to interchange the two factors. In particular a proof for (f,id) gives the corresponding proof for (id,f); composing these proves the general pair. The lemma asserts equality of the counit-defined maps, so this step never assumes invertibility of an arbitrary square mate.

source.place: alpha: composition and factor symmetry

proof.text:
For smooth f:X→Y and F=f×id_Z, put omega_f=G_f A_Y and let r:X×Z→X. The tensor isomorphisms theta and dualizing base-change isomorphism b of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness](1),(3) give
G_f K⊠Q → F^*(K⊠Q)⊗r^*omega_f → F^*(K⊠Q)⊗omega_F → G_F(K⊠Q).
All three arrows are isomorphisms. By [lem-sf-kv-smooth-transpose] their composite equals the specified alpha_{f,id}; hence that map is invertible for arbitrary K,Q. Treat pure relative dimensions on the open-and-closed components separately. The orientation is the diagonal/DNC one: [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity] and [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] identify this same tensor map with the smooth twist/shift purity map.

source.place: alpha: smooth purity and the specified transpose

proof.text: The finite etale/pro-etale transport used for triangles is exact monoidal. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives the monoidal comparison for the site morphism nu and the constant coefficient ring; [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] makes its inverse image exact. [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] identify the finite constructible finite-Tor objects on the two sites. Thus the etale tensor exactness [lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated] applies to the exterior tensor operations here.

source.place: alpha and beta: exact monoidal site transport

proof.text: Let i:C→Y be closed, j its open complement, and I=i×id_Z, J=j×id_Z. [prop-sf-localization-all-stages] gives the two supported triangles, one for K and one for K⊠Q. Externally tensor the first with Q; it stays distinguished by Step 6. At A=A_{E,n} on separated schemes the operations of [lem-sf-supported-external-triangle-comparison] (those of def-trf-admissibility, i.e. the exceptional inverse image of def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image) are the finite-level operations of sk-def-sf-operations (vi), and its alpha is the same counit-defined transpose. That lemma gives a morphism of triangles, connecting square included, with components RI_*(alpha_{i,id})∘c_i, the identity, and c_j. The ordinary product maps c_i, c_j are isomorphisms by [lem-trf-ordinary-kunneth]. Hence [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the first component invertible, so RI_*(alpha_{i,id}) is invertible. The unit T→I^!I_*T is invertible by [prop-sf-closed-unit-all-stages]. Consequently I_* reflects isomorphisms: apply I^! to an inverse and conjugate by these units. Therefore alpha_{i,id} is invertible.

source.place: alpha: closed immersions by a genuine morphism of localization triangles

proof.text: In the regular smooth pairs singled out by the unit, [sk-thm-regular](c) supplies Ri^!A=A_C(-c)[-2c], and (d) identifies the class of the product regular immersion with the exterior product of the two classes. The first comparison in [lem-sf-supported-external-triangle-comparison] is the specified counit transpose, so under these class normalizations it is the fundamental-class product comparison. Here both the smooth ambient and regular closed schemes required by sk-thm-regular are imposed. Regularity is used only for this normalization, not for the general closed-immersion argument in Step 7.

source.place: alpha: fundamental-class normalization in the regular case

proof.text: For a possibly nonseparated finite-type corner choose affine V⊂Y and affine W⊂f^{-1}V; also cover Z by affine opens. [lem-sf-kv-affine-locality] identifies the restriction of the specified alpha with that of f|_W:W→V on these charts. For W=Spec B, V=Spec R, B is a finitely generated R-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]; choose generators. The surjection R[t_1,...,t_r]→B makes W→A^r_V a closed immersion by the affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its composite with the projection A^r_V→V, smooth of pure relative dimension r by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], is f|_W. The smooth and closed cases, and [lem-sf-kv-alpha-transpose-coherence], make alpha invertible on every such product chart. The cone has zero cohomology sheaves on a covering, hence each cohomology sheaf is zero by the sheaf axiom; the cone is zero. Composition and factor symmetry now give alpha for every pair (f_1,f_2).

source.place: alpha: affine factorization and open detection

proof.text: The locality statement is used on its Noetherian, compactifiable domain: a field is Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes every finite-type corner Noetherian. Such a space is quasi-compact, and intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact because every open in a Noetherian space is quasi-compact. [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] therefore supplies compactifications of f and all its restricted maps. A finite subcover of the product charts exists. On these separated charts [thm-sf-ctf-stability](v) gives bounded constructible exceptional values with finite Tor intervals. The finite-cover clause of [lem-sf-kv-affine-locality] gives their global preservation, with the minimum lower and maximum upper bounds. Thus no separatedness of the original corners was added.

source.place: alpha: hypotheses for nonseparated corners and finite-cover preservation

proof.text: Source error (STATEMENT-DISPUTED, proof inference only): the imported reduction takes a closed immersion with source supp L. For j:G_m→A^1 and L=j_!A, the nonzero-stalk support is G_m, which is not closed. Taking its closure would require saying so. Steps 5-10 instead use the same smooth/closed/affine route, with arbitrary auxiliary coefficients already in the localization calculation. They establish alpha before the invalid support reduction is needed. The theorem statement is unchanged.

source.place: alpha: documented correction of the invalid support inference

proof.text: For beta at finite A, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] gives exactness with the signed shifts in each source variable E_i. Exterior tensor is exact by Step 6. The evaluation transpose [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](iii) respects these exact structures. Hence the isomorphism locus in each E_i is triangulated by [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three], and stable under retracts by retracting the inverse. Apply [sk-lem-sf-flat-model] successively in the two variables: it suffices to prove beta for E_i=Rh_{i!}F_i with h_i locally closed and F_i lisse with finite-projective local models. These generators are in D^b_ctf.

source.place: beta: exactness and finite-ring generation

proof.text: Each such F_i, in degree zero, is site-perfect: locally it is a direct summand of a finite sum of coefficient units. The finite datum was verified in Steps 2-3, so [prop-sf-dualizable-hom] gives the canonical evaluation isomorphism RHom(F_i,T)=F_i^vee tensor^L T. For the exterior-dual identity one may check on a cover where each F_i is an idempotent summand of A^{r_i}: Hom(A^r,T)=T^r respects the differential; taking the two idempotent summands gives (F_1⊠F_2)^vee=F_1^vee⊠F_2^vee. These are evaluation identities, hence agree on overlaps and glue. No general constructible object is assumed site-perfect, and no finite trivializing cover for an adic lisse object is used.

source.place: beta: site-perfect finite-projective evaluation

proof.text:
Set T_i=F_i^vee⊗^Lh_i^!L_i. By [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] and Step 13, RHom(E_i,L_i)=Rh_{i*}T_i. These objects are finite-Tor constructible by [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. Apply [sk-lem-sf-kunneth-star] first with f=h_1, auxiliary Rh_{2*}T_2 on Y_2:
Rh_{1*}T_1⊠Rh_{2*}T_2 → R(h_1×id)_*(T_1⊠Rh_{2*}T_2).
Apply it a second time with f=h_2, auxiliary T_1 on S_1, and factor symmetry:
T_1⊠Rh_{2*}T_2 → R(id×h_2)_*(T_1⊠T_2).
Both arrows are isomorphisms. Applying R(h_1×id)_* to the second and using [fix-prop-adjunctions](3) identifies the result with Rh_*(T_1⊠T_2), h=h_1×h_2.

source.place: beta: two separately typed ordinary Kunneth arrows

proof.text: Put F=F_1⊠F_2 and L=L_1⊠L_2. The monoidal pullback comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] and the exterior-dual identity identify T_1⊠T_2 with F^vee⊗^L(h_1^!L_1⊠h_2^!L_2). Apply Rh_*(1⊗alpha), which is invertible by Step 9, then finite-projective evaluation and [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] to reach RHom(Rh_!F,L). Ku_! in [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](i) identifies Rh_!F with E_1⊠E_2. Every arrow is invertible. [lem-sf-kv-beta-kunneth-evaluation] says this composite equals the specified evaluation-defined beta. Thus beta is invertible on the generators; Step 12 proves it for all E_i on separated schemes.

source.place: beta: invertible generator chain and equality with the specified map

proof.text: On products of affine opens in possibly nonseparated Y_i, the slice-restriction isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and monoidal restriction [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identify both endpoints and the evaluation transpose with beta on the separated charts. Its cone has zero cohomology on a covering, hence globally by the sheaf axiom. This proves beta on the full finite-coefficient domain.

source.place: beta: nonseparated corners by slice restriction

proof.text: At integral coefficients, [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii) gives finite reductions of internal Hom and exceptional inverse image preserving evaluation and adjunction maps. [lem-fix-operation-reduction], [fix-lem-exchanges] and [fix-prop-projection-formula] give reductions of pullback, tensor and the constituent compact-support product maps. Substituting into the definitions [sk-def-sf-kv-maps] shows that the reductions of the specified alpha and beta are the finite-level alpha and beta. Their cones are derived-complete constructible by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated]. Since all finite reductions vanish, the defining Roos triangle of [def-weil-derived-complete] has the form C→0→0→C[1]; hence C=0. Both integral maps are invertible.

source.place: coefficient passage: canonical reductions and complete cones

proof.text: At E the operations and their maps are scalar localizations by [lem-fix-operation-reduction] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; localizing each integral inverse gives an inverse. At Qbar choose a common finite coefficient field containing the finitely many input fields; the common-stage construction in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the map transports in [thm-sf-ctf-stability](vii) and [lem-fix-operation-reduction] represent the comparisons and their inverse there. They define inverse pairs over Qbar. In an idempotent completion restrict the inverse to the same idempotent summands. No rational object is reduced modulo a uniformizer.

source.place: coefficient passage: localization, common finite stages and retracts

proof.text: For a nonseparated corner apply the coefficient arguments on the finite affine covers already used. The normalized-system construction of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi) defines exceptional restriction levelwise by the finite open-adjoint comparisons of [lem-sf-kv-affine-locality]; its finite-cover clause gives uniform bounds. Pullback and tensor restriction are the same coefficient-tower constructions [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and internal Hom restricts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Thus the chart maps reduce to those already proved. Their complete cones vanish on the charts, then globally since their cohomology sheaves vanish on a cover. Localization and common-stage scalar extension preserve these inverse pairs.

source.place: coefficient passage: open restriction at all stages

proof.text: At each coefficient stage apply beta to (E_1,L_1)=(Lambda_X,M) and (E_2,L_2)=(N,omega_Y). The tensor-unit identities identify its source with M boxtimes D_Y N and its first target with RHom(p_Y^*N,M boxtimes omega_Y). The isomorphism alpha_{id_X,a_Y} identifies M boxtimes omega_Y with Rp_X^!M. Applying RHom(1,-) and composing gives exactly kappa of [sk-def-sf-kv-maps](iv). Both factors are isomorphisms, so kappa is an isomorphism. Naturality in every variable follows from the evaluation transposes defining beta and from the counit transposes defining alpha: both Hom bijections are natural, so transposing a natural composite gives a natural map. Composition and coefficient transport preserve these specified maps, as checked above. Empty schemes or a zero input give zero objects on both sides, so these edge cases require no dimension or support convention.

source.place: kappa: beta at (unit,M),(N,omega), followed by RHom(1,alpha)
